# Icons

shadshiny ships a small, curated icon set drawn from
[Lucide](https://lucide.dev) — enough to cover the components without
pulling in a font or an icon package. Reference an icon **by name**
anywhere a component takes an `icon` argument, or render one directly
with
[`shad_icon()`](https://orijitghosh.github.io/shadshiny/reference/shad_icon.md).

> Icon names are validated. Passing a name that isn’t in the set below
> throws an error rather than rendering nothing, so typos surface
> immediately.

## Using icons

``` r

shad_icon("search")                                   # a bare 16×16 SVG
shad_button("Search", icon = "search")                # leading icon
shad_button(icon = "plus", size = "icon")             # icon-only button
shad_badge("Verified", icon = "check")                # in a badge
shad_menu_item("mail", "Send mail", icon = "mail")    # in a menu
shad_sidebar_item("inbox", "Inbox", icon = "mail")    # in the sidebar
```

Get the full list programmatically with
[`shad_icon_names()`](https://orijitghosh.github.io/shadshiny/reference/shad_icon_names.md).

## The set

Every icon in the package, at its native size. The name under each is
exactly what you pass to `icon =`.

## Sizing & colour

Icons inherit the current text colour (`currentColor`), so they tint
themselves to whatever context they sit in — wrap one in a coloured
element and it follows. They render at `1rem` by default; to resize a
standalone icon, pass an inline `style` through `...` (it overrides the
default sizing), or attach the `shad-icon--sm` / `shad-icon--lg` class.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)
![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)
![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Code


    tags$span(style = "color:var(--shad-primary)", shad_icon("circle-check"))
    tags$span(style = "color:var(--shad-destructive)", shad_icon("triangle-alert"))
    shad_icon("loader", style = "width:2rem;height:2rem")

## Missing an icon?

The set is intentionally minimal. For anything outside it, pass your own
SVG (or any tag) wherever an `icon` argument is accepted — the
constructors take a tag just as readily as a name:

``` r

custom <- htmltools::tags$svg(
  xmlns = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", viewBox = "0 0 24 24",
  width = "16", height = "16", fill = "none", stroke = "currentColor",
  `stroke-width` = "2", htmltools::tags$path(d = "M12 2v20M2 12h20")
)
shad_button("Custom", icon = custom)
```
